sections.heading: HARD TO KILL
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 1 Hero Point You are hard to kill. You can be killed, but it would take something extreme, like being beheaded, dissolved in acid, or tossed into a volcano. Although Heroes can’t die in standard P&P, characters with this power know they’re hard to kill and can be roleplayed that way. When playing a game in which Heroes can die, GMs should charge more for this power (anywhere from 3 to 6 Hero Points).

sections.heading: HEALING
sections.text: Touch • Power Rank • 1 Hero Point per rank You can heal the injuries of anyone you touch. Your Power rank equals the maximum number of points of damage you can heal per day. The GM may also let this Power cure diseases with a successful Healing roll or perhaps by spending Resolve. CON Repair (−2): Your touch repairs inanimate objects rather than heals living beings. It can heal damage inflicted on androids, cyborgs, machines, robots, vehicles, and most other technology.

sections.heading: HIBERNATION
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 1 Hero Point You can enter a state of suspended animation and remain that way as long as you wish. You barely age and don’t need to breathe, eat, or drink anything while hibernating. You remain fully aware of your surroundings in this state and can revive yourself anytime you wish.

sections.heading: HYPER BREATH
sections.text: Special • Power Rank • 1 Hero Point per rank You can inhale and exhale gale-force winds that can pull things toward you or push them away from you. This requires a successful Hyper Breath roll against the greater of each target’s Might or weight rank. With 1 or 2 net successes, a target can be pulled to you or pushed out to Distant Range. With 3 or more net successes, the target also falls prone and loses their next turn to act. This power can either affect all targets within Close Range or a single target within Distant Range. You can also use Hyper Breath to disperse gasses or inhale and hold them as long as you can hold your breath, but this doesn’t grant you any special immunity to caustic or toxic gasses. PRO Freezing (+1 per rank): You can also use your breath to freeze targets, mimicking the effects of Blast (cold) or Ensnare, but only within Close Range.

sections.heading: ILLUSIONS
sections.text: Zone • Power Rank • 1 Hero Point per rank You can create illusions. Your illusions can be as small as you like, or they can fill the Power’s area of effect with illusory sights and sounds. Your illusions exist in the real world and can be perceived by both living beings and inanimate objects like cameras and microphones. Observers will believe your illusions are real unless they have a reason to think otherwise, in which case they can make a Perception roll against your Power rank to see through them. Whether or not they believe them, anyone who attempts to touch your illusions will pass right through and immediately realize they aren’t real. If you place an illusion over a physical object, however, merely touching it won’t give anything away because the observer will touch the object underneath. PRO Mental (+2 per rank): You create illusions in the minds of living beings. Observers who have a reason to believe your illusions aren’t real use Willpower rather than Perception when trying to see through them. Although your illusions can’t be detected by inanimate objects like cameras and microphones, they are more effective on living beings, who can be made to believe they have been blinded, bound, gagged, harmed, incapacitated, immobilized, or otherwise affected by some part of the illusion. Whatever the trappings, these illusory special effects all basically work like the Stun Power, but using your Illusions rank against the target’s Willpower. Although your illusions can cover a large area, as described above, you can only target single individuals with illusory special effects like these unless you apply the Zone Pro.

sections.heading: IMMORTALITY
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 3 Hero Points You can’t die or you don’t stay dead. Maybe you always come back to life, maybe your consciousness gets transferred into a clone or duplicate body, etc. However it works, killing you doesn’t stick. What’s more, you won’t grow old or die of old age, at least not within any time frame that matters. Although Heroes can’t die in standard P&P, characters with this power know they can’t die and can be roleplayed that way. When playing a game in which Heroes can die, GMs should charge more for this power (anywhere from 6 to 12 Hero Points). CON Vulnerable (−1): You can be killed, but it’s not an easy thing to do. Describe how.

sections.heading: IMMUNITY
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 3 Hero Points per immunity You are immune to certain attacks, conditions, effects, energies, hazards, or Powers. Select one or more of the following immunities or make up your own. • Attack X: You are immune to a specific type of physical attack or weapon. • Energy X: You are immune to a specific type of energy other than kinetic/physical energy. • Environmental: You are immune to environmental hazards like pressure, radiation, and temperature. • Fatigue: You never tire or get mentally fatigued and you don’t need to rest or sleep. • Life Support: You don’t need to breathe, eat, or drink, and you are immune to airborne toxins. • Mental States: You are immune to negative emotions and mental states like fear and confusion. • Sensory: You are immune to the Dazzle Power and similar sensory overload effects. • Toxins: You are immune to diseases, drugs, and poisons.

sections.heading: INANIMATE
sections.text: Self • Special • 9 Hero Points You aren’t alive, at least not in the usual sense. You might be a construct, a robot, undead, or something else. You are immune to physical attacks and Powers that only affect living beings, whether those Powers are harmful or helpful. Additionally, you effectively have Immunity (Life Support, Toxins). You still have a mind or spirit, so you remain vulnerable to mental attacks and Powers. This Power has no rank and can’t be absorbed, drained, mimicked, or affected by other abilities. It does have a Source (other than Trained) which suggests what kind of being you are, as follows: • Innate: you are a living being, but not in any way that resembles life on Earth. • Magic: you are a supernatural being like an angel, devil, elemental, faery, golem, or undead. • Psychic: you are an astral or ectoplasmic being like a ghost or spirit and are likely incorporeal. • Super: you are inorganic matter or energy brought to life by some inexplicable phenomenon. • Tech: you are an artificial construct like a clockwork being, nanoswarm, robot, or sentient program. PRO Mindless (+9): You are also immune to mental attacks and Powers because you lack both mind and spirit, as in the case of a true robot or a magically animated skeleton or zombie.

sections.heading: INVISIBILITY
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 9 Hero Points You can turn invisible. You can still be detected by other senses, by Powers like Attuned, Radar, and Super Senses, and by how you affect the environment (footprints in mud or snow, the movement of fog or rain, etc.). Enemies who can’t see you suffer a −3d penalty to their attack rolls and active defense rolls against you unless they have a Power like Blind Fighting or Radar that compensates for this. Lower this penalty to −2d for enemies that can detect you as described above, even if they can’t see you. PRO Cloaking (+3): When you turn invisible, you also become undetectable to Radar and all Super Senses that involve vision. Additionally, you become undetectable to sensors and other equipment (magical, technological, or otherwise) that operates like these Powers. CON Jamming (−3): You can’t turn invisible, but you can render yourself undetectable to Radar and all Super Senses that involve vision. Additionally, you become undetectable to sensors and other equipment (magical, technological, or otherwise) that operates like these Powers.

sections.heading: IRRITANT
sections.text: Zone • Power Rank • 1 Hero Point per rank You can fill the area around you with an effect like a blinding sandstorm, hurricane force winds, noxious gas, or a swarm of insects. Everyone in the area other than you suffers a −2d penalty to all challenge rolls (other than passive defense rolls) unless their Toughness exceeds your Power rank. If you wish, you can specify that your version of the Power is resisted with Willpower instead of Toughness. You must use an action to activate this Power, but once you do, you can maintain it as a free action.

sections.heading: LANGUAGES
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 1 Hero Point All characters can speak one or two languages, but you speak a number of extra languages equal to your Intellect. You can select these languages ahead of time or during play. PRO Hyper Translation (+2): You are instantly fluent in any language you encounter. You can’t speak languages your vocal cords can’t mimic, or understand ones your senses can’t perceive. PRO Polyglot (+1): You have a natural talent for languages. You can master new languages in about a week or so and can normally learn enough to get by within a day or two.

sections.heading: LEADERSHIP
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 6 Hero Points You lead your team in battle. As long as you can see and communicate with them, you can spend a free action to let each of your allies reroll one challenge roll per combat scene.

sections.heading: LEAPING
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (½ Might) • 1 Hero Point per rank This Travel Power lets you jump incredible distances, as shown on the Leaping table. Subtract 1d from your Power rank to determine how high you can jump straight up. Leaping can be used to travel long distances like any other Travel Power. This Power works best outdoors because it requires overhead clearance. As a result, your Leaping rank is capped at your Agility when making movement rolls indoors. Last, you can also use Leaping as an active defense against falling damage.

sections.heading: LIFE DRAIN
sections.text: Touch • Power Rank • 2 Hero Points per rank You can drain the life of any living being you touch by making a Life Drain roll against their Toughness or one of their active defenses. If you wish, you can specify that your version of the Power is resisted with Willpower instead of Toughness, but active defenses will always apply as well. You inflict 1 point of damage per net success rolled. If you are wounded, you also heal 1 point of damage for every 2 full points of damage inflicted. For example, you heal 1 point of damage whenever you inflict 2 or 3 points of damage. You don’t have to be wounded to use this Power. PRO Vampirism (+1): Rather than merely draining life energy, the Power inflicts actual physical damage so targets resist this Power like they would any ordinary attack that inflicts physical damage (using Armor, half their Toughness, or an active defense). Because the Power inflicts physical damage, it can be used to attack inanimate objects and beings. Nevertheless, you only heal damage when the Power is used on living targets.

sections.heading: LIGHT/EFFECT
sections.text: Special • Default Rank • 3 Hero Points You can generate light, normally visible light but you can generate ultraviolet light if you prefer. This is effortless and always considered a free action. Your light can fill the Zone around you, or you can focus it down to a beam or a harmless laser that extents to Distant Range. The light can be as bright as you like, but not so bright that it incapacitates others like Dazzle. That said, suddenly going from total darkness to bright light will probably stun just about anyone, if only for a moment. Although Light is the most common version of this ability, this Power can instead represent the ability to generate some other innocuous but useful environmental effect (in which case it’s called Effect to avoid confusion).

sections.heading: LIGHTNING REFLEXES
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 3 Hero Points You have incredible reflexes. Increase your Edge by 6. Also, while this is mostly for narrative flair, you can draw, holster, or sheathe any weapon you carry in an instant. If using the Gritty Combat Rules in Chapter 4, this makes it impossible for anyone to get the drop on you. CON Fighting/Marksmanship (−1): This Power only applies when performing close combat attacks or ranged combat attacks, respectively, and you can only quick draw those types of weapons.

sections.heading: LUCK
sections.text: Self • Power Rank • 2 Hero Points per rank You are incredibly lucky or so skilled that you make everything look easy. You gain a number of Luck dice equal to your Luck rank at the start of every issue. Luck dice can be added to either side of any challenge roll that involves you. For example, you can spend 3 Luck dice to add +3d to one of your challenge rolls. You can also spend 3 Luck dice to oppose the roll of someone acting against you. In that case, you roll the dice, count your successes, and subtract them from the other person’s roll. Much like when you spend Resolve, this happens automatically, without you needing to do anything. PRO Control (+4): Rather than just being lucky, this Power represents your ability to consciously alter probability fields. This lets you use Luck on yourself and anyone you wish within Distant Range. Although you have to be conscious and aware, using this Power is considered a free action, and you can do so at any time—you don’t have to wait for your turn to act. PRO Unbelievable (+1 per rank): You can also spend Luck dice to buy yourself lucky breaks, as described in Chapter 5. Lucky breaks purchased with Luck dice are often more extreme, spectacular, and unlikely than those purchased with Resolve. Of course, they’re still subject to the GM’s approval and can’t be used to break the game.

sections.heading: MACHINE CONTROL
sections.text: Ranged • Power Rank • 1 Hero Point per rank You can control machines and electronic devices at up to Distant Range. For example, you can use this Power to hack into a computer, deactivate a security camera, or remotely control a car. You can also substitute your Power rank for whatever Trait you’d normally use to operate the machine or device. You can control multiple machines at the same time, but every extra machine controlled lowers your effective Power rank by 1d, and you still suffer the usual −2d penalty if you use the Power to perform multiple attacks or actions in combat. CON Interface (−2): You can only control computers. However, this also lets you control any machine or device controlled by a computer, which covers a lot of ground.

sections.heading: MARTIAL ARTS
sections.text: Touch • Baseline Rank (Might) • 1 Hero Point per rank You are a master of unarmed combat. You can use this Power to perform and defend yourself against close combat attacks. You can also substitute your Martial Arts rank for your Might when performing and resisting grabs, holds, escapes, and combat stunts. You’ve also trained with weapons and can substitute your Martial Arts rank for your Ability ranks when using mundane melee weapons to attack or defend yourself (although the Gear Limit for mundane weapons still applies, as discussed in Chapter 6). Unlike most attack Powers, Martial Arts inflicts subdual damage (although you still inflict lethal damage when armed with a melee weapon that inflicts such damage). PRO Deflect (+4): You can deflect ranged attacks. This lets you use Martial Arts as an active defense against ranged physical and energy attacks, but not against area attacks. PRO Deflect Missiles (+2): You can deflect ranged attacks. This lets you use Martial Arts as an active defense against ranged physical attacks, but not against area attacks.

sections.heading: MASTER OF DISGUISE
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 3 Hero Points You are a master of disguise. You can create extremely realistic disguises in one short scene or less, assuming you have on hand whatever materials and supplies you need (and in a pinch, you can do wonders with ordinary household goods). You are also a master of mimicry, able to imitate the voice and mannerisms of others. Use Charm when making challenge rolls for this ability, typically opposed by your target’s Perception. When the Item Con is applied to this Power, it must mean something more than just needing materials and supplies to craft your disguises because that is assumed.

sections.heading: MATTER CHAMELEON
sections.text: Self • Power Rank • 2 Hero Points per rank You can take on the properties of objects you touch for the rest of the scene. This works like Solid Form, but your effective Power rank equals the lesser of your Matter Chameleon rank or the Structure of the object. You also take on the energetic properties of objects you touch, such as the heat of lava, gaining Aura at the lesser of your Matter Chameleon rank or the rank of the energy coming off the object. You suffer no damage from this unless the energy’s rank exceeds your Power rank, and even then, this Power acts as a passive defense against energetic damage inflicted by touching objects.

sections.heading: MIND BLAST
sections.text: Ranged • Power Rank • 1 Hero Point per rank You can fire a mental attack that targets the mind or spirit, inflicting psychic damage on living beings by making a Mind Blast roll against your target’s Willpower. This Power has no effect on inanimate objects and in fact goes right through them unless they have a psychic presence.

sections.heading: MIND CONTROL
sections.text: Ranged • Power Rank • 2 Hero Points per rank You can make any living being within Distant Range do what you wish for the Power’s duration by making a Mind Control roll against their Willpower. You can control your target immediately, or you can spend 1 Resolve to implant suggestions that will be triggered at some point in the future (possibly months or even years later, in which case the duration won’t begin to run until the suggestion is triggered). Targets get a +2d bonus to resist commands that are totally against their natures or selfdestructive. CON Hypnosis (−2): You need to have a calm, face-toface conversation with anyone whose mind you want to control, making this ability useless in combat. CON Pheromones (−2): Your Power is chemical in nature. Characters use the greater of their Toughness or Willpower to resist it. Additionally, characters who don’t breathe are immune to this Power, as are those protected by life support systems or immune to toxins.

sections.heading: NULLIFY
sections.text: Zone • Power Rank • 2 Hero Points per rank You can create a dampening field that nullifies the Abilities, Talents, and Powers of all characters within range, friend and foe alike. Nullified Abilities and Talents drop to 1d, while nullified Powers completely stop working. You can only nullify Traits if your Power rank equals or exceeds their rank, but this happens automatically: no roll is required. This Power only affects Traits from one Source (pick one). You have to concentrate to use this ability—you can only move at half speed, and you can’t attack, use active defenses, or perform other actions while this Power is active unless you spend 1 point of Resolve to do so. A target affected by this Power may spend Resolve to muscle their way through and use a nullified Trait, but each page or use of a nullified Trait will cost them 1 point of Resolve. PRO Also X (Special): You can affect Traits from more than one Source. Every additional Source increases this Power’s cost by 1 Hero Point per rank. For example, this Power costs 4 Hero Points per rank if you can nullify Innate, Super, and Trained Traits.

sections.heading: OMNI-POWER
sections.text: Special • Power Rank • 3 or 5 Hero Points per rank You possess a versatile ability that lets you mimic other Powers at this Power’s rank. You can mimic any number of Powers per page, and you can switch between them in an instant, but each use of this Power after the first on the same page lowers your effective Omni-Power rank by 1d for the rest of that page. For these purposes, a “use” is any action, movement, or challenge roll involving this Power. Pandora is using her 12d Omni-Power to fly over the city (mimicking Flight). The demon she’s hunting bursts out from the clouds above her, shrieking as it dives in her direction, so she blasts it with a bolt of arcane energy (mimicking Blast). This is the second use of Omni-Power on the same page, so Pandora rolls only 11d for her attack roll. She defeats the creature, but it wasn’t alone. Two lesser fiends appear out of nowhere and attack Pandora on the same page. Pandora raises an arcane shield to protect herself (mimicking Armor). These are the third and fourth uses of Omni-Power on the same page, so Pandora rolls only 10d and 9d for her defense rolls against the two attacks. This reduction concerns how often you use this Power in one page; it has nothing to do with how many actions you perform. Accordingly, if you use this Power to perform 2 or more attacks on the same page, you also suffer the usual multiple action penalty on your attack rolls (see Chapter 4). Powers with a default rank can only be mimicked if your current Omni-Power rank equals or exceeds their cost in Hero Points. For example, you need at least 3d Omni-Power to mimic Light because that Power costs 3 Hero Points. Omni-Power cannot be used to mimic Alternate Form, Determination, Inanimate, Life Drain, Luck, Nullify, Power Absorption, Power Mimicry, Preparation, Slay, or Time Stop. You can apply Pros to the Powers you mimic by spending 1 Resolve per Pro, or 2 Resolve for Pros that cost at least 4 Hero Points. If you spend Hero Points to apply a Pro to this Power overall, you can apply it to any Power you mimic without spending Resolve. Cons can only be applied to this Power overall, and affect all Powers you mimic. For example, if you apply the Signature Con to this Power, every Power you mimic will have the Signature Con. There are two types of Omni-Powers: narrow and broad. Narrow Omni-Powers can imitate a limited set of abilities, and cost 3 Hero Points per rank. Broad Omni-Powers can imitate a wide array of abilities, and cost 5 Hero Points per rank. You must describe what your Omni-Power does when you select it so that both you and your GM understand what it can and can’t do. This is especially important for broad Omni-Powers, which often do many things but should never let you do everything. Use the examples below as a guide. GMs are free to limit or prohibit this Power. • Arsenal (narrow): You carry a collection of arrows, boomerangs, bullets, grenades, shuriken, etc., that let you imitate Powers that inflict damage and special effects. • Gadgets (broad): You carry an assortment of technological wonders that you can use to imitate the effects of a wide variety of Powers. • Gizmos (narrow): You wear a utility belt or pack, or perhaps you have items built into your body. This lets you imitate Powers that represent a wide variety of mundane tools and miscellaneous equipment. • Quantum Control (broad): You can control matter and energy at the quantum level, and probably have some control over time and space as well. • Sensors (narrow): Common among high-tech characters, you have an advanced sensor suite that can imitate the effects of most Super Senses involving hearing or vision. • Sorcery (broad): You are a practitioner of the arcane arts who uses your vast magical knowledge to create an assortment of magical effects that are somehow related.

sections.heading: PHASING
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 9 Hero Points You can shift your body out of phase with the physical world. This makes you immune to physical attacks and effects (including energy attacks), but not to mental ones. It also allows you to pass through solid objects, but not through force fields. You can’t carry, touch, or affect anything physical while phased. Activating or deactivating this Power is a free action, but you cannot do both on the same turn to act (use Blink to represent the ability to quickly activate and deactivate this Power in combat). PRO Intangible (+3): Normal force fields can’t hold you, but those with the Ward Con can, unless your Willpower exceeds their Power rank.

sections.heading: PLASTICITY
sections.text: Self • Power Rank • 2 Hero Points per rank Your body is rubbery and elastic, allowing you to mold yourself into different shapes and squeeze through the tightest openings. You can create different effects at your Plasticity rank by shaping yourself into different forms. For example, you can imitate Leaping by shaping yourself into a ball, you can use Plasticity instead of Might to hold something in place by winding or wrapping yourself around it, or you can use yourself as a parachute for anything with a weight rank less than or equal to your Power rank. In combat, you can use Plasticity as a passive defense against physical attacks, but not against energy attacks, and you can substitute Plasticity for Might when grappling or performing close combat attacks. If your Might exceeds your Power rank, use Might +1d instead.

sections.heading: POLYMORPH
sections.text: Ranged • Power Rank • 1 Hero Point per rank You can turn living beings into some harmless or helpless form (a frog, a sheep, a statue, whatever) by making a Polymorph roll against their Toughness or one of their active defenses. If you wish, you can specify that your version of the Power is resisted with Willpower instead of Toughness, but active defenses will always apply as well. The target transforms for the Power’s duration. Some Villains and Foes may have versions of this Power that last much longer, even permanently!

sections.heading: PORTABLE STOREHOUSE
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 6 Hero Points You can access a storehouse of mundane weapons, armor, gear, and even vehicles from wherever you are. This might involve teleporting these things to and from a secret warehouse, pulling them out of a magic bag or hat, carrying them around in shrunken form, creating them out of thin air, or something else entirely. These items only last until the end of the scene, unless you have Resources or Wealth, in which case you may very well be using this Power to grab your own items out of storage.

sections.heading: POSSESSION
sections.text: Ranged • Power Rank • 1 Hero Point per rank You can possess the body of living beings within Distant Range by making a Possession roll against your target’s Willpower. While possessing someone, you use their physical Abilities, Talents, and Powers and your mental Abilities, Talents, and Powers (it’s the GM’s call). While you are using this Power, your physical body lies dormant, but you will instantly know if it gets moved or harmed. You automatically jump back to your own body if the person you are possessing gets knocked out or killed. PRO Meld (+4): Your body melds into that of anyone you possess for the power’s duration.

sections.heading: POWER ABSORPTION
sections.text: Touch • Power Rank • 2 Hero Points per rank You can steal a character’s Abilities, Talents, and Powers from a specific Source (pick one) by making a Power Absorption roll against their highest-ranked Trait that shares this Source or one of their active defenses. If successful, your target falls unconscious and you gain the stolen Traits at their rank for the Power’s duration. If you already have a stolen Trait at an equal or greater rank, your Trait is unaffected. You can possess the Traits of multiple characters at the same time, but this lowers your effective Power rank by 1d per extra character. If used on a Minion whose abilities come from the correct Source (it’s the GM’s call), you gain an attack and defense rank equal to their Threat if that’s better than what you would normally use. This Power requires physical contact, so it can’t affect anyone completely hidden behind artificial armor or a force field. PRO Also X (Special): You can absorb Traits from more than one Source. Every additional Source increases this Power’s cost by 1 Hero Point per rank. For example, this Power costs 4 Hero Points per rank if you can absorb Innate, Super, and Trained Traits. CON Only X (−2 or −4): You can only absorb one type of Trait. This is usually a −2 Con and means you can only affect Abilities, Talents, or Powers (pick one). If you can only absorb one specific Ability, Talent, or Power (again, pick one), this is a −4 Con instead.

sections.heading: POWER MIMICRY
sections.text: Touch • Power Rank • 2 Hero Points per rank You can mimic a character’s Abilities, Talents, and Powers from a specific Source (pick one) by making a Power Mimicry roll against their highest-ranked Trait that shares this Source or one of their active defenses. If successful, you gain the mimicked Traits at their rank for the Power’s duration. If you already have a mimicked Trait at an equal or greater rank, your Trait is unaffected. This does not affect your target in any way. You can possess the Traits of multiple characters at the same time, but this lowers your effective Power rank by 1d per extra character. If used on a Minion whose abilities come from the correct Source (it’s the GM’s call), you gain an attack and defense rank equal to their Threat if that’s better than what you would normally use. This Power requires physical contact, so it can’t affect anyone completely hidden behind artificial armor or a force field. PRO Also X (Special): You can mimic Traits from more than one Source. Every additional Source increases this Power’s cost by 1 Hero Point per rank. For example, this Power costs 4 Hero Points per rank if you can mimic Innate, Super, and Trained Traits. CON Only X (−2 or −4): You can only absorb one type of Trait. This is usually a −2 Con and means you can only affect Abilities, Talents, or Powers (pick one). If you can only absorb one specific Ability, Talent, or Power (again, pick one), this is a −4 Con instead.

sections.heading: PRECOGNITION
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 12 Hero Points You can rewrite events that have already happened, perhaps because you can see into the future, predict the most likely outcome of any course of action, or actually turn back time. However this works, you can spend Resolve to negate something that just happened in the game. In combat, this erases a character’s turn and lets you skip your normal place in the action sequence and immediately take your next turn to act before they repeat theirs. You must declare this as soon as a character finishes their turn to act, if not sooner. Once another character begins to act, you can’t go back any farther than the start of the acting character’s turn. This costs 1 Resolve the first time you use this Power in a scene, 2 Resolve the second time, 3 Resolve the third time, and so on. Characters are not refunded Resolve or Adversity spent during an erased turn. GMs should feel free to disallow this Power.

sections.heading: PREPARATION
sections.text: Self • Special • 6 Hero Points Thanks to your penchant for meticulous research and planning, you tend to be prepared for any situation. As discussed in Chapter 5, all Heroes can spend 1 Resolve to make up some minor detail about the game world, often a lucky break that works in their favor. This Power lets you take that one step further, making these narrations much more effective if they can be explained by your research and planning. This allows you to declare that you are carrying the perfect item, tool, or mundane weapon (assuming your gear hasn’t been taken from you), that you planted something in or otherwise prepared your current location ahead of time, that you already know or have access to information you need, or that you know or have pull with some Extra. Preparation isn’t an instant win button you can use to narrate your way around every challenge or obstacle the GM throws your way. Even with this Power, the GM can veto any narration they consider unreasonable or game-breaking. This Power has no rank and can’t be absorbed, drained, mimicked, or affected by other abilities. Vigilant has this Power. While chasing the crystalline supervillain Shard through the city’s sewer system, Vigilant spends 1 Resolve to say that he memorized the layout of the city’s sewers long ago. Knowing this, he manages to get ahead of Shard, who rounds a bend to find the city’s dark protector waiting for him. Massively strong and impervious to most weapons, Shard isn’t impressed. After all, Vigilant’s just a guy in a costume. Shard charges at him, expecting to pound him into jelly. Our hero spends 1 more Resolve to declare that he’s done his research on Shard and knows all there is to know about him. Since Shard’s been in and out of jail a few times, the GM agrees, and she discloses that Shard is vulnerable to sonic and vibratory attacks. Vigilant spends 1 final point of Resolve to declare that, having discovered this, he temporarily added vibrating knuckles to his costume’s armored gauntlets. For the duration of this scene, his unarmed attacks will inflict vibratory damage. One well-placed uppercut later and Shard is on his back, knocked unconscious by just a guy in a costume.

sections.heading: PSI-SCREEN
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (Willpower) • 1 Hero Point per rank You’ve honed your mental and spiritual defenses. Use Psi-Screen instead of Willpower when defending yourself against mental attacks and resisting mental damage and effects. Also, you know when someone tries to use Telepathy to read your surface thoughts, and you can use this Power to resist such attempts. You can also use this Power to resist attempts to probe your mind. PRO Cloak Mind (+2): You can hide your mental presence from telepaths. Anyone who wants to use Telepathy to detect you must make a successful Telepathy roll against your Psi-Screen rank.

sections.heading: PSYCHOMETRY
sections.text: Touch • Default Rank • 9 Hero Points You can pick up psychic impressions and glean information from physical objects. You can ask the GM about the basic history of any inanimate object you touch. If you spend 1 Resolve, you can ask for in-depth information about a specific person or event connected to the object, assuming there’s any information to be had. The information received may sometimes be incomplete or misleading, but it is always truthful and must address the subject of your question.

sections.heading: QUICK CHANGE
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 3 Hero Points You can change your attire and/or grooming (hairstyle, makeup, etc.) in an instant. Describe how this works. Using this Power takes an action. CON Costume (−1): You can only change into your costume or into what you were wearing (if anything) when you last changed into your costume.

sections.heading: RADAR
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 3 Hero Points You have some kind of radar sense that provides a threedimensional image of your surroundings. This doesn’t let you see flat images like print, pictures, or video displays. CON Sonar (−1): This Power only works underwater. CON Tremor Sense (−1): Rather than using radar, you are sensitive to vibrations in the ground. You can only detect beings and objects that are in contact with the ground or causing the ground to vibrate, as might be the case with low-flying helicopters or VTOL jets.

sections.heading: REGENERATION
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 6 Hero Points You recover from injuries very quickly: you heal 1 point of damage per hour. If you get knocked unconscious, you awaken as soon as you heal 1 point of damage (if not revived sooner). PRO Fast (+6): You heal 1 point of damage per minute instead of per hour. PRO Instant (+18): You heal 1 point of damage per page instead of per hour.

sections.heading: RESISTANCE
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (Toughness) • 1 Hero Point per 2 ranks You are resistant to radiation, temperature extremes, and toxins (diseases, drugs, and poisons). Use this Power instead of Toughness when rolling to resist hazards like these.

sections.heading: RUNNING
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (3d) • 1 Hero Point per rank This Travel Power lets you run faster than normal. This can also represent rolling on wheels, skating, or even bouncing like a ball. This Power’s 3d baseline rank reflects standard human running speed. PRO Hover (+2): You hover up to 1 foot above the ground when using this Power. This allows you to ignore caltrops, pressure plates, squeaky floors, tripwires, uneven ground, and so on.

sections.heading: SEPARATION
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 3 Hero Points You can detach your body parts without the usual side effects like screaming and bleeding to death. Your detached parts act independently and can generally do whatever a detached but otherwise healthy body part might reasonably be able to do, taking your other Powers into account. For example, a detached hand can crawl around on the ground, manipulate objects, and scare the hell out of people. If you can fly, then your hand probably can too.

sections.heading: SHOCKWAVE
sections.text: Zone • Power Rank • 1 Hero Point per 2 ranks You can generate a concussive wave that targets everyone within range, friend and foe alike. This requires a successful Shockwave roll against the greater of each target’s Might or weight rank. With 1 or 2 net successes, a target is pushed away from you and suffers a −1d penalty to all challenge rolls until after your next turn to act. The target remains within Close Range of you, but they’re no longer adjacent to you if they were beforehand. With 3 or more net successes, the target is also knocked prone and loses their next turn to act. This Power shatters fragile materials like ordinary glass and ice in its area of effect.

sections.heading: SHRINKING
sections.text: Self • Power Rank • 2 Hero Points per rank You can shrink, becoming as small as shown on the Shrinking table and lowering your weight rank by your current Shrinking rank until it reaches 0d. You can substitute your current Shrinking rank for your Agility. You also gain Leaping and Strike at half your current Shrinking rank. If you already have any of these Traits at an equal or greater rank, use their ranks +1d instead. As discussed in Chapter 4, your size may also make it easier to hit others and avoid the attacks of human-sized enemies.

sections.heading: SHRINKING — RANK HEIGHT RANK HEIGHT
sections.text: 1d to 2d 3 feet 13d to 14d ½ inch 3d to 4d 2 feet 15d to 16d ¼ inch 5d to 6d 1 foot 17d to 18d ⅛ inch 7d to 8d 6 inches 19d to 20d Flea-sized 9d to 10d 3 inches 21d to 22d Mite-sized 11d to 12d 1 inch 23d to 24d Microscopic

sections.heading: SLAY
sections.text: Touch • Power Rank • 2 Hero Points per rank You can harm living targets you touch by making a Slay roll against their Toughness or one of their active defenses. If you wish, you can specify that your version of the Power is resisted with Willpower instead of Toughness, but active defenses will always apply as well. You inflict 2 points of damage per net success rolled. Armor has no effect on this Power.

sections.heading: SLICK
sections.text: Zone • Power Rank • 1 Hero Point per rank You can make all or any portion of the ground within range slippery for the rest of the scene or until you dispel this effect. Anyone attempting to cross the slick must make an Agility roll against your Power rank to avoid falling. Characters who fail this roll fall prone. Attempting to stand requires an action and another Agility roll against your Power rank. Until they make this roll, characters caught in the slick can’t leave the area, at least not on foot, and suffer a −2d penalty to their attack rolls and active defense rolls. A character driving a ground vehicle over the slick must make a Vehicles roll against your Power rank to keep from sliding out of control and crashing into something.

sections.heading: SPEAK WITH DEAD
sections.text: Self • Power Rank • 2 Hero Points per rank You can momentarily animate the bodies of the dead to speak with them. This lets you ask the deceased your Power rank number of questions which must be answered truthfully. The dead will know only what they did while they were alive and can only communicate in a language they knew. As you might imagine, you need a dead body (or at least a head) to use this Power.

sections.heading: SPECIALTY
sections.text: Self • Special • 0 Hero Points This Power is only available in Street Level and Low Level games, typically ones involving Heroes who lack true superpowers and share similar backgrounds, characteristics, and/or training. It provides niche protection that helps differentiate characters who might otherwise be too similar, such as a group of adolescent mutant ninja critters or a paramilitary group of True American Heroes. This Power allows each Hero to excel at something unique to them. The basic combat and non-combat Specialties are described below, but you are encouraged to create your own. This Power has no rank and can’t be absorbed, drained, mimicked, or affected by other abilities. When playing a game using Specialties, each Hero selects one Specialty for free (notice that this Power costs 0 Hero Points). No Hero can have more than one Specialty, and each Hero must have their own. In some games, GMs may let Heroes select two Specialties, one combat Specialty and one non-combat Specialty (again, no two Heroes can have the same Specialty). Your Specialty does two things. First, you get a +1d bonus to certain types of challenge rolls, even if this bonus effectively pushes you over the game’s Trait Cap. Second, when making these rolls, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode. That means you get to roll those dice again to try generating extra successes, and you get to keep rerolling them as long as you keep rolling 6s.

sections.heading: COMBAT SPECIALTIES
sections.text: • Acrobat: You get a +1d bonus to movement rolls and active defense rolls. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls. • Blaster: You get a +1d bonus to ranged attack rolls. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls. • Grappler: You get a +1d bonus to grappling rolls of any kind. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls. • Striker: You get a +1d bonus to close combat attack rolls. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls. • Support: You get a +1d bonus to rolls made to perform combat stunts (see Chapter4). Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls. • Tank: You get a +1d bonus to Toughness rolls, Willpower rolls, and passive defense rolls. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls.

sections.heading: NON-COMBAT SPECIALTIES
sections.text: • Detective: You get a +1d bonus to Investigation rolls and Streetwise rolls. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls. • Driver/Pilot: You get a +1d bonus to Charm rolls and Vehicles rolls. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls. • Executive: You get a +1d bonus to Command rolls and Professional rolls. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls. • Explorer: You get a +1d bonus to Academics rolls and Survival rolls. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls. • Face: You get a +1d bonus to Charm rolls and Professional rolls. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls. • Infiltrator: You get a +1d bonus to Covert rolls and Investigation rolls. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls. • Journalist: You get a +1d bonus to Charm rolls and Investigation rolls. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls. • Mechanic: You get a +1d bonus to Technology rolls and Vehicles rolls. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls. • Medic: You get a +1d bonus to Medicine rolls and Science rolls. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls. • Scholar: You get a +1d bonus to Academics rolls and Investigation rolls. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls. • Scientist: You get a +1d bonus to Investigation rolls and Science rolls. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls. • Scout: You get a +1d bonus to Covert rolls and Survival rolls. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls. • Soldier: You get a +1d bonus to Command rolls and Survival rolls. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls. • Techie: You get a +1d bonus to Science rolls and Technology rolls. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls. • Thief: You get a +1d bonus to Covert rolls and Streetwise rolls. Additionally, you can spend 1 Resolve to have your 6s explode when making these rolls.

sections.heading: SPINNING
sections.text: Self • Power Rank • 1 Hero Point per rank You can spin along your axis at superhuman speed. This lets you use Spinning in place of Might when performing and defending yourself against close combat attacks, grabs, holds, escapes, and combat stunts. You can also use Spinning in place of Agility when defending yourself against physical attacks, but not against energy attacks. If your Abilities are of equal or greater rank, use their rank +1d instead. You can move, speak, and interact with others normally while spinning.

sections.heading: STAR GATE
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 3 Hero Points You can instantly transport yourself to distant worlds. Although it involves travel, you must spend an action to use this Power. The first time you travel to an unfamiliar world, you arrive at a random location determined by the GM. After that, you return to where you were when you left, or you can spend 1 Resolve to arrive at another familiar location of your choosing. You can use this Power a number of times per issue equal to your Willpower without paying anything. Each use after that costs 1 Resolve. PRO Portal (+2): You can create portals through which others (including ships) can travel.

sections.heading: STRETCHING
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 1, 3 or 6 Hero Points You can stretch, telescope, or extend your body, or maybe you have long reach. You can perform close combat attacks and grappling attacks against targets that aren’t adjacent to you. The 1-point version of this Power lets you reach targets within Close Range. The 3-point version lets you reach targets within Distant Range. The 6-point version lets you reach targets within Extreme Range. Out of combat, these distances indicate about how far you can reach or stretch yourself. CON Long Reach (−1): You have long reach but can’t stretch your whole body.

sections.heading: STRIKE
sections.text: Touch • Baseline Rank (Might) or (Martial Arts) • 1 Hero Point per rank You have some kind of damaging close combat attack like claws, energized fists, or a unique melee weapon. You can use this Power to both perform and defend yourself against close combat attacks. You must specify the kind of damage inflicted when you buy this Power (unless you apply the Weapons Con (discussed below). Occasionally, a more descriptive term may be used when the Power inflicts physical damage. For example, Strike (Bite) or Strike (Claws) may be used in place of Strike (Physical). This is purely for flavor and has no mechanical effect. PRO Deflect (+4): You can deflect ranged attacks. This lets you use Strike as an active defense against ranged physical and energy attacks, but not against area attacks. PRO Deflect Missiles (+2): You can deflect ranged attacks. This lets you use Strike as an active defense against ranged physical attacks, but not against area attacks. PRO Reach/Throw (+2): The Power can be used against opponents who aren’t adjacent to you, as long as they’re within Close Range. Either the Power has unusually long reach (Reach) or you can somehow throw whatever you use to attack enemies in close combat (Throw). PRO Sweep (+4): The Power can be used as an area attack that targets all characters in a 90-degree arc within 5 to 25 feet of you. Like all area attacks, this targets both friend and foe within the area of effect. If the Power also has Reach, you can affect targets up to 50 feet away. You decide how far the attack reaches each time you use this Pro. CON Subdual (−1): This Power inflicts subdual damage. CON Weapons (−1): This Power represents mastery of a group of weapons as broad or narrow as you like—the level of specificity doesn’t matter. You must be armed with that type of weapon to use the Power. This lets you use your Strike rank (instead of your Ability plus Weapon Bonus) to make attack rolls and defense rolls against close combat attacks while so armed. Otherwise, the weapon works as usual and deals whatever type of damage it normally inflicts.

sections.heading: STUN
sections.text: Ranged • Power Rank • 1 Hero Point per rank You can incapacitate a living opponent by disabling them, stunning them, paralyzing them, putting them to sleep, or doing anything else that takes them out of the action by making a Stun roll against their Toughness or one of their active defenses. If you wish, you can specify that your version of the Power is resisted with Willpower instead of Toughness, but active defenses always apply as well. CON EMP (−2): The Power affects characters with the Inanimate Power from a Tech Source instead of living beings. It can also disable most devices with electronic components.

sections.heading: SUMMONING
sections.text: Self • Power Rank • Special You can animate, call, or summon Minions to do your bidding. Your Power rank determines how many Minions you can summon per scene, as shown on the Summoning table. You determine your Minions’ Threat rank when you purchase this Power. You can select any rank up to the game’s Trait Cap - 6d, unless you can summon no more than 10 Minions per scene, in which case you can select any rank up to the game’s Trait Cap - 3d. This Power costs 1 Hero Point per rank for every 2d Threat you give your Minions (round up as always). For example, if your Minions have 5d or 6d Threat, this Power costs 3 Hero Points per rank. Summoned Minions are close combat fighters unless you apply the Shooters Pro (see below). Summoning Minions is an action, but your Minions can act on the page in which they appear.

sections.heading: SUMMONING — RANK MINIONS
sections.text: 1d to 2d 2 3d to 5d 5 6d to 8d 10 9d to 11d 25 12d to 14d 50 15d to 17d 100 18d to 20d 250 21d to 23d 500 24d to 26d 1,000 PRO Animals (+1 or +2 per rank): Your Minions are animals, so they possess special abilities like enhanced senses and the ability to move faster than ordinary human beings. Work with your GM to make up the specifics depending on the kind of animals you can summon. This Pro costs +1 per rank if you can summon a narrow selection of animals or +2 per rank if you can summon a wide variety of animals with different special abilities. PRO Automatons (+1 per rank): Your Minions have the Inanimate (Mindless) Power. PRO Duplicates (+2 per rank): Your Minions are duplicates of you. Although they work like ordinary Minions and use their Threat for all attacks, defenses, and other challenge rolls, your duplicates share your unique abilities and can do things other Minions can’t. For example, if you can fly, phase through walls, or shoot energy beams out of your eyes, your duplicates can do so as well. Having a large number of duplicates can have significant narrative benefits (shortening the time of a long project considerably; searching an entire building in moments; highly efficient disaster relief; etc.) so discuss expectations with your GM before selecting this Pro. PRO Shooters (+1 per rank): Your Minions can also attack enemies within Distant Range. PRO Unique (+1 to +4 per rank): Your Minions have unique abilities that would be represented by Powers if they weren’t Minions, things like acute senses, flight, or the ability to walk through walls. Work with your GM to describe what your Minions can do. This Pro costs +1 per rank if it gives your Minions a minor advantage, +2 per rank if it gives them a moderate advantage, or +4 per rank if it gives them a major advantage. This Pro is subject to the GM’s approval.

sections.heading: SUPER SENSES
sections.text: Your senses are enhanced in some way. Select all the following that apply. Regardless of the options you select, Super Senses is always considered a single Power with an effective rank equal to your Perception or your Acute X rank, whichever is greater.

sections.heading: ACUTE X
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (Perception) • 1 Hero Point per 2 ranks One of your senses is hyper acute (pick one). Substitute your Acute X rank for you Perception when making challenge rolls involving that sense (but not when determining your Edge).

sections.heading: ANALYTIC X
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (Perception) • 1 Hero Point You can use one of your senses (pick one) to determine the basic physical properties of anything you concentrate on, including chemical composition and whether something is organic or inorganic.

sections.heading: ASTRAL SIGHT
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (Perception) • 1 Hero Point You can see into the astral realm, the realm of psychic energy tied to the physical world. Among other things, this lets you interact with invisible spirits and characters using Astral Projection. It also lets you detect camouflaged living beings who are using Powers like Blending or Invisibility.

sections.heading: CIRCULAR VISION
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (Perception) • 1 Hero Point You effectively have a 360-degree field of view.

sections.heading: ENHANCED HEARING
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (Perception) • 1 Hero Point You can detect extremely faint, distant, or muffled sounds impossible for ordinary humans to hear by making a Perception roll at a threshold of 4 or higher, as determined by the GM depending on the circumstances. Additionally, you can hear infrasound and ultrasound.

sections.heading: HYPERSENSITIVE TOUCH
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (Perception) • 1 Hero Point Your sense of touch is sensitive enough to read print with your fingertips or discern what’s happening in an adjacent room by feeling the vibrations through a door or wall.

sections.heading: LIE DETECTION
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (Perception) • 3 Hero Points You can detect when someone within Close Range is lying. You might need to make a Perception roll if the person is somehow protected from this Power, but otherwise this is automatic.

sections.heading: MICROSCOPIC VISION
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (Perception) • 1 Hero Point If you concentrate, you can see microscopic details, maybe even down to the atomic, subatomic, or quantum level. In short, you can achieve whatever level of magnification the story requires.

sections.heading: NIGHT VISION
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (Perception) • 3 Hero Points Through whatever means, you can see in absolute darkness.

sections.heading: RADIO HEARING
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (Perception) • 1 Hero Point You can hear radio frequencies and intercept radio transmissions.

sections.heading: TELESCOPIC VISION
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (Perception) • 1 Hero Point You can make out small details at extremely long distances. As with Microscopic Vision, you can basically see as far as you need to for purposes of the story.

sections.heading: THERMAL VISION
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (Perception) • 2 Hero Points You can see heat patterns, allowing you to see through thin objects and follow even the faintest traces of residual thermal energy. This also lets you see in the dark, but it can be foiled by things like extreme ambient temperatures and beings whose body temperatures match their surroundings precisely.

sections.heading: TRACKING SCENT
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (Perception) • 1 Hero Point You can identify, recognize, track others, and even determine their emotional state by scent. These feats require Perception rolls at a threshold of 4 to 6 under optimal conditions.

sections.heading: TRUE SIGHT
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (Perception) • 6 Hero Points If you concentrate, you can see a being’s true form, penetrating disguises, illusions, and transformations of any kind, including Powers like Blending and Invisibility. You might need to make a Perception roll if the person is somehow shielded from this effect, but otherwise this is automatic.

sections.heading: ULTRA VISION
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (Perception) • 2 Hero Points You can see in ultraviolet light, which is normally invisible to the human eye. You also have low-light vision, allowing you to see in lighting as dim as starlight, but not in absolute darkness.

sections.heading: X-RAY VISION
sections.text: Self • Baseline Rank (Perception) • 6 Hero Points If you concentrate, you can see through solid objects.

sections.heading: SUPER SPEED
sections.text: Self • Power Rank • 3 Hero Points per rank You move at superhuman speed. This works like any other Travel Power and then some. You can run at Power rank speed, your Agility effectively equals your Super Speed rank, and your Edge equals your Super Speed rank times 3. You can use this Power to perform and defend yourself against close combat attacks. You can also substitute Super Speed for Might when defending yourself in grappling combat. If you have Super Speed at 9d or greater, you gain a number of benefits: you can cross 2 range classes per page in combat, you can run across water and up walls, you defeat 2 Minions per net success when targeting them in close combat, and you effectively gain the Quick Change and Vanish Powers. You can compare your speed to the 10 mile-per-hour speed of an ordinary person to gauge how fast you really are and how quickly you can perform mundane tasks. For example, 9d Super Speed lets you run 1,000 miles per hour, making you roughly 100 times faster than an ordinary human being.

sections.heading: SWIMMING
sections.text: Self • Power Rank • 1 Hero Point per 2 ranks This Travel Power lets you move through water at great speeds. Additionally, you can breathe water, you move as freely underwater as you do through air, your senses are not impaired underwater, and you are immune to oceanic pressure and temperature. CON Lungs (−1): You can’t breathe water, but you can hold your breath for a long time.

sections.heading: SWING LINE
sections.text: Self • Power Rank • 1 Hero Point per 2 ranks This Travel Power allows you to ascend, descend, and swing from place to place. It only works outdoors or in large indoor areas with enough overhead space for you to swing around. You must remain within Distant Range of buildings, tall trees, or other stable objects to which you can tether your swing lines. Your lines have a Structure equal to half your Power rank. If you have Swing Line at 7d or greater, something more than simple gravity is propelling you from place to place. CON Natural (−2): You can’t create your own swing lines, so this Power only works in jungles and other environments that provide you with natural lines such as vines.

sections.heading: TELEKINESIS
sections.text: Ranged • Power Rank • 2 Hero Points per rank You can move objects at up to Distant Range with your mind. Use your Telekinesis rank as your effective Might when doing so. You can use this Power to attack, immobilize, lift, and toss beings and objects around. Telekinesis can also be used as an active defense against ranged attacks. Ranged physical attacks can be affected directly, but ranged energy attacks have to be blocked with physical objects—use the lesser of your Telekinesis rank or the Structure of the shielding object (or the Body of the shielding vehicle) when using this Power to defend yourself against energy attacks. You can control multiple objects at one time, but this lowers your effective rank by 1d per extra object controlled, and you still suffer the usual multiple action penalties if you perform more than one action per page. CON Impel (−4): You can move objects in a straight line or hold them in place, but fine manipulation and subtle control is beyond you.

sections.heading: TELEPATHY
sections.text: Ranged • Power Rank • 1 Hero Point per rank You can read minds and transmit your thoughts to anyone within Distant Range. You can sense sentient minds within range, but other telepaths can cloak their mental presence if they wish. You must make an opposed Telepathy roll against a cloaked telepath to sense them. You can also read a person’s surface thoughts by making a Telepathy roll against the higher of their Willpower or Telepathy rank, although telepaths can sense this. Last, you can probe a person’s memories for specific information by making a Telepathy roll against the higher of their Willpower or Telepathy rank. This takes a few minutes of absolute concentration, and even non-telepaths can feel when someone is digging through their memories. A successful mind probe reveals regular memories, repressed memories, and even original memories that have been altered in some way and can be restored if desired. PRO Alter Memories (+6): Whenever you roll 3 or more net successes while performing a mind probe, you can alter a subject’s memories however you wish. These alterations are temporary, lasting the rest of the scene, but if you spend 1 Resolve, you can make them permanent. PRO Cloak Others (+2): You can cloak the mental presence of everyone within Close Range of you, making their minds undetectable to this Power (as described above). PRO Dream Travel (+2): You can enter, observe, and participate in the dreams of others. While in a dream, your physical Traits are replaced by the greater of your Willpower or Telepathy rank. PRO Mind Link (+2): You can link a number of minds equal to your Power rank so that everyone can telepathically communicate with everyone else. Linked characters must remain within Extreme Range of you to access the mind link. CON Empathy (−2): Your telepathic abilities are limited to sensing, reading, and transmitting emotions and mental states, but stop short of concrete things like words and images.

sections.heading: SUPER TIP!
sections.text: Time Stop and Time Travel can be excellent in certain players’ hands and absolutely gamebreaking in others. We include them for the sake of being complete, but urge GMs to think carefully before letting Heroes have either ability.

sections.heading: TELEPORTATION
sections.text: Self • Power Rank • 1 Hero Point per rank You can instantly travel as far as shown on the Teleportation table. You can teleport through solid objects, but not through force fields. You have no trouble reaching places you can see or locations whose layout you know well. If you try teleporting to an unfamiliar place, roll two dice. A result of 6 or less means you almost teleport into a solid object, so the Power fails. When that happens, you reappear in your original location and the shock knocks you unconscious for the rest of the scene (you can spend 1 Resolve to remain conscious). Each use of this Power is a move, no matter how far you travel. However, you can spend 1 Resolve to teleport twice in one page, provided you use 1 action and the total distance covered doesn’t exceed the maximum distance you can teleport.

sections.heading: TELEPORTATION — RANK DISTANCE
sections.text: 1d to 2d 50 feet 3d to 5d 500 feet 6d to 8d 1 mile 9d to 11d 10 miles 12d to 14d 100 miles 15d to 17d 1,000 miles 18d to 20d Planetary 21d to 23d Orbital 24d to 26d Lunar PRO Portal (+2): You can create portals through which others can travel. CON Medium (−2): You can only teleport along or through a medium such as along power lines, through shadows, or into and out of reflective surfaces.

sections.heading: TIME STOP
sections.text: Zone • Power Rank • 3 Hero Points per rank You can stop the flow of time in the Power’s area of effect for a number of pages equal to your Power rank or until you dispel this effect. This costs 1 Resolve the first time you use this Power in a scene, 2 Resolve the second time, 3 Resolve the third time, and so on. While this Power is active, everyone and everything in the area is frozen, stuck in time. You can move around freely while this Power is in effect, and you can move objects and people around (assuming you are strong enough to do so), but you can’t otherwise affect or harm anything stuck in time. Although energy and forces affect you while this Power is active, they don’t affect anyone or anything else. For example, you can’t defy gravity or walk across lava while this Power is active, but you can place an object in mid-air or in a fire, and the object will sit there, hovering in the air or untouched by the flames, until time begins moving again. You can also do something like place a live grenade at someone’s feet and then dispel the Power. This is another Power GMs should feel free to disallow if they don’t want to deal with the potential for abuse.

sections.heading: TIME TRAVEL
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 3 Hero Points You can travel through time, forward or backward, as far as you like. Although it involves travel, you must spend an action to use this Power. Time Travel can be a major headache, so discuss this Power with your GM ahead of time. If the GM approves, they’ll have to determine how time travel works, including the age-old question of whether you can change the present by altering the past (we highly recommend Kevin Kulp’s amazing TimeWatch roleplaying game published by Pelgrane Press for some great ideas on all things time travel). GMs are free to impose whatever restrictions they wish on this Power. PRO Portal (+2): You can create portals through which others can travel.

sections.heading: TOTAL RECALL
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 3 Hero Points You automatically remember anything you pay attention to, and you can make an Intellect roll against whatever threshold the GM decides to see if you noticed specific background details as well. PRO Playback (+1): Typically found among cyborgs and robots, your memories can be transferred, stored, copied, and displayed for others.

sections.heading: TRACER
sections.text: Touch • Default Rank • 3 Hero Points You can tag objects you touch with a tracer. Once tagged, you can follow objects anywhere in the world for the rest of the story. You might need to make an Intellect roll if the object moves to a location that somehow blocks this Power, but otherwise this is automatic. A person who suspects they’ve been tagged can search for your tracer, but finding it requires a Daunting (3) Perception roll. PRO Tracking (+3): If you have an object that recently belonged to a subject or you visit a location the subject visited within the last day or so, you can track them as if they’d been tagged.

sections.heading: TRANSFORMATION
sections.text: This Power lets you turn yourself into other things. The details vary depending on which version of this Power you have. Regardless of which Transformation Power you possess, changing form is always a free action, but you can only do so on your turn to act unless you forego you next turn to act.

sections.heading: ANIMAL FORMS
sections.text: Self • Power Rank • 2 Hero Points per rank You can turn into animals, gaining their appearance, form, size, and weight. You also gain their Agility, Might, Perception, and Toughness and their Powers at the lesser of their rank or your Power rank. You can turn into any natural animal you are familiar with, whether alive or extinct. As for magical creatures like dragons and unicorns, that’s up to the GM. If you are an alien, you turn into alien animals. For the sake of game balance (and everyone’s sanity), these alien animals look different but have the same characteristics as the Earth animals described in Chapter 8. PRO Enhanced (+4): Whenever you turn into an animal, you can use your Power rank in place of its highest ranked Trait. You can do this for only one Trait per animal (pick one if several Traits have the same rank). For example, gorillas have 6d Might and Toughness. If you use 10d Animal Forms to turn into a gorilla, you can give yourself 10d in one of those Abilities. CON Only X (−2 or −4): You can only turn into a specific category, group, or type of animal specified when you buy this Power. This is normally a −2 Con, but if you can only turn into a single animal or an extremely limited group of animals, this becomes a −4 Con instead.

sections.heading: DOPPELGANGER
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 6 Hero Points You can turn into an exact duplicate of anyone you’ve ever seen, even aliens, as long as they’re roughly humanoid in shape and not too much larger or smaller than you. You can fool biometric scanners and even DNA analysis, but you don’t gain any of the subject’s Abilities, Talents, or Powers.

sections.heading: OBJECT FORMS
sections.text: Self • Power Rank • 2 Hero Points per rank You can turn into objects, from simple geometric shapes to mundane tools and weapons to complex machines and vehicles. By turning into simple shapes, you can exert Power rank force or resistance. By turning into tools and weapons, you can add half your Power rank to the challenge rolls of anyone using you as a tool or the attack rolls of anyone using you as a weapon, up to a maximum rank equal to your Power rank. By turning into machines and vehicles, you gain their characteristics at the lesser of their rank or your Power rank. Although this doesn’t affect your Traits, you can alter your size significantly when using this power, making yourself as large or as small as if you had the Growth and Shrinking Powers at this Power’s rank.

sections.heading: SHAPESHIFTING
sections.text: Self • Power Rank • 2 Hero Points per rank You can reshape your gross physical form however you like. You have a number of Hero Points equal to your Power rank that can be used to temporarily raise your physical Abilities (Agility, Might, and Toughness) and to buy Powers that represent things like claws, extra limbs, fins, gills, spines, tentacles, tough hide, wings, and so on. No Trait can have a rank that exceeds the game’s Trait Cap. For purposes of determining your Resolve (as discussed in Chapter 5), this Power’s effective rank equals your Shapeshifting rank plus the greatest of your Agility, Might, or Toughness ranks.

sections.heading: TRANSMUTATION
sections.text: Touch • Power Rank • 2 Hero Points per rank You can alter the chemical composition of inanimate matter that you touch. You can automatically affect gas within Close Range of you. To affect liquids or solids, you must make a Transmutation roll against the greater of their Structure or weight rank. By transforming elements and compounds, you can raise their Structure up to your Power rank or lower it as much as you wish, going as far as turning solids into liquids or gases, and vice versa. If you create energetic or harmful substances like chlorine gas, lava, or uranium, use your Power rank as their effect rank. These effects last for the rest of the scene or until you dispel them, but you can spend 1 Resolve to make them permanent if you wish. You also have to spend 1 Resolve to create elements and compounds that are unique to the game world or that have unique effects, such as magical metals or incredibly rare minerals that render a mighty superhero powerless because they’re fragments of his home planet that exploded long ago.

sections.heading: TUNNELING
sections.text: Self • Power Rank • 1 Hero Point per rank This Travel Power lets you travel by digging your way through the ground. You can collapse your tunnels behind you or leave them open for others to follow. You don’t give any indication of your passage to those above ground, making this a great way to surprise your enemies.

sections.heading: TWO-DIMENSIONAL
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 6 Hero Points You can become two-dimensional, like a shadow (whether you take on the appearance of a black silhouette is up to you). This renders you weightless and silent, but you can still affect and be affected by the three-dimensional world as usual. In addition to moving normally through three-dimensional space, you can also slide along any surface, ignoring gravity while doing so, and slip through any crack wide enough to fit your form while using this Power.

sections.heading: TWO-FISTED
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 3 Hero Points You use both hands in combat. You can spend 1 Resolve to defeat twice as many Minions as usual (2 per net success rolled) when making a physical attack. You can decide whether to spend the Resolve after making your attack roll. This Power applies to all physical attacks, but it provides no additional benefit to attacks that already work this way (i.e., area attacks, Super Speed attacks, and attacks involving the Ricochet Pro). If you happen to be dual wielding mundane weapons, you can also increase their Weapon Bonus by +1d. This bonus applies only to mundane weapons, not to Powers with Cons like Item or Weapons. To be clear, this Power does not grant extra attacks. CON Fighting/Marksmanship (−1): This Power only applies in close combat and the bonus to mundane weapons applies only to melee weapons (Fighting), or it only applies in ranged combat and the bonus to mundane weapons applies only to ranged weapons (Marksmanship).

sections.heading: VANISH
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 3 Hero Points You can vanish from sight in the blink of an eye and move as far as you can in one page without anyone seeing where you went. This often happens under the cover of a blinding flash or a puff of smoke. Using this Power requires both 1 action (to vanish) and movement (to move elsewhere).

sections.heading: VARIANT
sections.text: Special • Special • 3 Hero Points This Power grants you a different version of another power you already have. Although you only spend 3 Hero Points to buy a Variant Power, it must be worth the same number of Hero Points as the original. For example, if you have Blast (Ice) 8d, you could also have a Blast Variant (Fire) 10d (Charges 3): the 8d Blast costs 8 Hero Points, while the Blast Variant is also worth 8 Hero Points because the Charges Con saves you the 2 extra Hero Points you would normally have to spend to buy the power at 10d instead of 8d. You can’t have a Variant of Alternate Form, Boost, Drain, Elemental Control, Nullify, Omni-Power, Power Absorption, Power Mimicry, or any other Power that affects other Traits.

sections.heading: VENTRILOQUISM
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 3 Hero Points You are a master of mimicry and ventriloquism. You can mimic almost any sound, imitate others effectively, and make your voice seem to come from another location. Use Charm when making challenge rolls for this ability, typically opposed by your target’s Perception.

sections.heading: WALL-CRAWLING
sections.text: Self • Power Rank • 1 Hero Point per 2 ranks You can stick to walls and ceilings and can move along them at your normal speed. If your Power rank is lower than your Might, use your Power rank to determine how much weight you can carry while wall-crawling. You might need to make a WallCrawling roll to stick to unusually slick or slippery surfaces.

sections.heading: WEAKNESS DETECTION
sections.text: Self • Default Rank • 3 Hero Points You can find the weak points of any person or object you observe in person. If you spend 1 Resolve, your physical and energy attacks effectively gain the Penetrating Pro against that person or object for the rest of the scene. Additionally, this Power can also provide you with narrative information about the structural integrity, flaws, and stress points of any object you study (this doesn’t cost Resolve).

sections.heading: SUPER TIP!
sections.text: A player who selects Weakness Detection has given the GM a gift that lets them throw all sorts of unique and otherwise unconquerable Villains at the Heroes (consider the classic video game Shadow of the Colossus).

sections.heading: PROS AND CONS
sections.text: The following section includes generic Pros and Cons. You can apply these options to existing Powers to create a wide variety of superpowers and unique abilities. Although the descriptions below generally refer to Powers, many Pros and Cons can also apply to Abilities, and some can even apply to Talents. The Pros and Cons provided below are not intended to cover every possible option, so feel free to make up your own.

sections.heading: AFFECT INANIMATE
sections.text: PRO +1 Hero Point This Pro applies to Powers that affect only living beings. It means the Power can also affect one type of inanimate being; in other words, characters with the Inanimate Power from one Source (pick one). You can apply this Pro multiple times to affect different types of inanimate beings.

sections.heading: AREA OF EFFECT
sections.text: PRO +1 to +4 Hero Points These Pros apply to Powers that only affect individual targets, turning them into Powers that target an area of effect. When targeting an area instead of an individual character in combat, you make a single attack roll and everyone in the area (whether friend or foe) makes their own defense roll. Area attacks are hard to evade, so active defense ranks are halved against them unless the defender foregoes their next turn to act leaping away or behind cover. The Pros are as follows. Area/Burst: These Pros apply to Ranged Powers. Area gives you the option of targeting an area or an individual character, while Burst means the power always targets an area. Either way, the area of effect can be anywhere from 10 to 50 feet in diameter. Area lets you vary the size of the area of effect each time you use the Power, but Burst requires you to specify the size of the area when you create the Power. Area costs +2 Hero Points and Burst costs +1 Hero Point. Zone/Nova: These Pros apply to Ranged Powers and Touch Powers. Zone gives you the option of targeting the area within 5 to 25 feet of you or an individual character. Nova means the power always targets the area within 5 to 25 feet of you. Zone lets you vary the size of the area of effect each time you use the Power, but Nova requires you to specify the size of the area when you create the Power. When applied to Ranged Powers, Zone costs +2 Hero Points and Nova costs +1 Hero Point. When applied to Touch Powers, these Pros cost twice as much, or +4 Hero Points and +2 Hero Points, respectively.

sections.heading: ARMOR PIERCING
sections.text: PRO +2 Hero Points This Pro applies to Powers that inflict physical or energy damage. It means the Power penetrates body armor with ease. Characters wearing mundane armor have their passive defenses halved against the Power. Active defenses are unaffected by this Pro. No Power can have this Pro and the Weak Con.

sections.heading: BUILD-UP
sections.text: CON −2 Hero Points The Power must build up over 2 pages before you can use it. You can’t use the Power on the first or second page of the action, but you can use it on the third page and every page after that.

sections.heading: BURNOUT
